newsitem.title: USA: Family gets $7 million in US cell-phone crash case.
newsitem.headline: Family gets $7 million in US cell-phone crash case.

text.p: A Texas jury ordered an 18-year-old girl on Tuesday to pay about $7 million in damages to the family of a boy killed when she lost control of her vehicle while answering a cellular telephone.
Kayla Segerstrom crashed her family van head-on into another car on Jan. 13, 1996, losing control when she reached to answer the telephone.
A three-year-old boy was killed in the accident. His baby sister's neck was broken and their father, James Colvin, suffered serious brain damage.

The Fort Worth jury awarded the Colvins about $7 million in damages. The family's attorney Steven DeWolf said about $5.5 million was awarded to cover medical treatment for James Colvin with $1 million awarded for the death of his son Cole and $200,000 for the neck injuries to his daughter, Briana.
Additional damages and charges took the total to about $7 million, he said.
The Colvins had sued Segerstrom and her parent's family company, which owned the van and cellular phone, but the jury ruled only against the girl.
DeWolf said the case was precedent-setting because it addressed the issue of responsibility in an accident caused by use of a cellular phone.

He had told the jury that Segerstrom's parents should have taught her how to use the phone safely. He said the phone's operating manual warned drivers to pull off the road if necessary before using it.
